_readme: Visual descriptions of PF2e ancestries, for image prompts only.
This lives in the tooling and NOT in lore/ancestries.md on purpose, for two
reasons. The lore file is feeling-first by convention (docs/ancestry-
conventions.md): it says what a people IS, the temperament and disposition,
and carries no appearance at all. And the appearance is not Tyrnarra's to
define anyway; these are Pathfinder 2e ancestries, described by Paizo.
Check anything doubtful against Archives of Nethys.
THREE STATES, and the difference matters:
""         the name alone is enough. An image model already draws this
one correctly, so adding words only spends prompt budget.
This is a FINDING, not a gap: it means somebody checked.
"text..."  the model does not know the ancestry, or knows a different
thing by that name, so the look has to be described.
absent     not catalogued yet. The builder warns rather than guessing.
Entries are short by design, 15 to 30 words. They are prepended to a spec's
`character` text, so they compete with it for the ~150-word Midjourney
budget, and the individual matters more than the species. A spec's own
`character` may contradict the catalog freely: a regional kitsune should not
be forced to look like every other kitsune.
Heritage and cosmology sections of lore/ancestries.md (Layer 1/2/3, mortal
mixes, the old powers' lines) are not ancestries and are not listed here.
_verify: Written from memory of PF2e and not yet checked against Archives of Nethys.
These are the ones worth a look before they reach a render:
athamaru, surki, yaksha, yaoguai, jotunborn, samsaran, sarangay, conrasu
anadi: a shapechanging spider-folk in humanoid form, four small dark eyes above the usual two, fine chitin at the knuckles and jaw, clothing of their own woven silk
android: a synthetic person, smooth even skin with faint circuitry seams tracing the temples and forearms, symmetrical features, steady luminous eyes
athamaru: a sea-dwelling folk, sleek skin in deep blue-grey, webbed fingers, a low finned crest instead of hair, wide dark eyes
automaton: a walking construct of dark brass and iron, articulated plate limbs with visible joints, a soft glow in the chest cavity, a faceplate rather than a face
awakened animal: an ordinary beast woken to personhood: upright, expressive-eyed, wearing cut-down clothing made for a body it was never meant to fit
azarketi: an amphibious person, smooth blue-green skin, webbed hands, gill slits along the neck, large dark eyes adapted to deep water
conrasu: a bodiless spirit wearing a carved shell of pale wood and living growth, no face inside the hood, faint light at the seams
dragonet: a small draconic person, fine overlapping scales, a short blunt snout, folded membranous wings, slit-pupilled eyes
fetchling: a shadow-touched person, ash-grey skin, colourless hair, eyes with no whites, edges that never quite catch the light
fleshwarp: a body remade by magic against its will, mismatched limbs, grafted features that do not share an origin, seams where they were joined
ghoran: a person grown rather than born, a body of woven vine and stem, petals and broad leaves for hair, a face suggested in the growth
goloma: a person whose head and shoulders are covered in many open eyes of different sizes, a short dense pelt over the rest
jotunborn: giant-blooded, very tall and heavy through the bone, blunt broad features, a head that does not fit a mortal-sized doorway
kashrishi: smooth faintly translucent crystalline skin in a single soft hue, and a large clear crystal horn rising from the centre of the forehead
kholo: hyena-folk, sloped powerful shoulders, a blunt muzzle, coarse spotted coat, a laugh built into the shape of the jaw
leshy: a small plant spirit in a made body of gourd, bark or bundled leaves, with a simple carved face and no skin beneath
nagaji: serpent-folk, fine scales across the skin, a flat snake-like nose and lidless eyes, a low hood of scale at the neck
poppet: a living doll of stitched cloth and stuffing, button eyes, visible seams at the shoulders and neck, patched where it has worn through
samsaran: pale blue skin, white hair, calm unlined features, faint markings across the brow left by lives it does not remember
sarangay: a bull-headed person, heavy horns, a short coat over powerful shoulders, and a single gem set into the centre of the forehead
shisk: pale grey skin and a long mane of stiff porcupine quills running from the crown down the spine, small dark eyes, a narrow face
shoony: small stout dog-folk, deeply wrinkled faces, long drooping ears, short limbs, a perpetually earnest expression
strix: a winged person, large dark feathered wings folded at the back, sharp angular features, hollow-boned and light
surki: an insectile person, a segmented chitin carapace in dull earth tones, compound eyes, fine antennae swept back from the brow
tanuki: raccoon-dog folk, round-faced and thick-furred, a broad striped tail, dark markings across the eyes
tripkee: frog-folk, smooth damp skin in vivid patterned colour, wide-set bulging eyes, long fingers with soft pads
vanara: monkey-folk, a fur-covered body and an expressive mobile face, a long prehensile tail carried high
vishkanya: fine jewel-toned scaling laid over otherwise human features, catching the light across the temples and the backs of the hands, eyes with a faint cold luminescence
wayang: a small shadow-touched folk, skin in flat greys and blacks that swallow light, angular features, no highlights anywhere on them
yaksha: a nature spirit wearing a person's shape, skin the colour of bark or river stone, small horns or budding growth at the brow
yaoguai: a beast that became a person and kept the evidence: a mostly human shape carrying the ears, eyes or hands of the animal it was
